kill_fact: The backlog-truth test lands where the bear said it would, and it is confirmed against the primary source rather than refuted: on the 2026-07-29 Q3 FY2026 earnings call the chief executive described the entire power-for-artificial-intelligence demand signal as customers who 'continue to increase their forecast for 2027, '28 and beyond into the early 2030s' and said that 'if all those cases are true, we'll have to expand capacity' - an explicitly conditional forecast, not an order book. Woodward disclosed no backlog figure, no book-to-bill ratio, no contracted volume and no counterparty beyond 'Rolls-Royce's mtu Solutions division' anywhere on that call; the only use of the word backlog on the call refers to the AIRFRAMERS' backlog, not Woodward's. The capacity decision was deferred again ('I think we'll be in a better position to talk about what that looks like at our Investor Day', 2027-03-04). Sizing the exposure the chain actually rests on: Industrial was $401M of $1,109.7M of Q3 revenue (36%), and power generation is one of four end markets inside it (power gen +19%, marine +24%, oil and gas +11%), so power-for-AI is a low-teens-percent slice of consolidated revenue while 64% of the company (Aerospace, $709M) sits outside this book's chain entirely. The thesis is not killed - the adverse case's own mechanism is verified, not fabricated - but the record's chain membership rests on an unbacklogged, twice-deferred forecast, which is exactly the SOFT_EXTENDED status it already carries.
corrections: Four fixes, none of which break the adverse case's arithmetic. (1) The adverse sum-of-the-parts does not foot: its own schedule of $12,600M Aerospace plus $3,192M Industrial less $2,720M capitalised corporate cost gives enterprise value of $13,072M, and $13,072M less $1.0B of net debt over 61.5M diluted shares is $196.3 per share, not the $195 printed - a 0.7% slip in the bear's own favour. The base case foots exactly ($19,920M + $5,950M - $3,570M = $22,300M, less $885M over 61.0M = $351.1) and needs no change. (2) Receivables are overstated: the record's '$1,056M' is the data-vendor aggregate, while the 10-Q line 'Accounts receivable and other, net' at 2026-06-29 is $1,012.5M - the $43.9M difference is income taxes receivable, not trade credit. Days of sales on trailing revenue of $4,192.0M is therefore 88 days, not 92. The cash-quality point survives intact because the chief financial officer conceded on 2026-07-29 that 'our accounts receivable balance at the end of the third quarter was higher than expected due to collections timing', and trailing free cash flow of $376.5M against trailing net income of $552.0M is a 68% conversion exactly as claimed. (3) Fiscal-2025 year-end net debt was $395.0M, not the 'roughly $391M' stated ($722.4M total debt including $20.2M of leases, less $327.4M of cash, at 2025-09-30); the 2.24x increase to $885.2M at 2026-06-30 is confirmed to the dollar. (4) The record is priced off $375.89 as at 2026-08-04; WWD closed at $356.55 on 2026-08-10, down 5.1%. That does not flip the risk_reward conclusion - the stock is still above the $351 base fair value - but the stated asymmetry is stale: distance to the favourable case is now +26.5% and to the adverse case -45.3%, a ratio of 1.7 times rather than the 'roughly 2.5 times' printed. Everything else in the adverse case verified verbatim or to the dollar: price realisation of 10% in the June quarter and 'close to 8%' for the year with 'between 3% and 5%' guided as the normal forward rate after the post-2022 long-term agreements closed out; the roughly 100 basis points of one-time retroactive Aerospace pricing; China on-highway at $40M in Q3 contributing about 90 basis points of Industrial segment margin with none expected in Q4; core Industrial guided back to first-half levels ('18% is nothing to sneeze at'); capital spending of $156M in nine months against a $290M full-year guide; the abandoned inventory-turn improvement; $602.0M of trailing-four-quarter repurchases against weighted diluted shares of 61,317K versus 61,374K (-0.09%) and basic of 59,632K versus 59,442K (+0.32%); 1.6x gross debt to earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation; and zero open-market insider purchases in every quarter from 2025Q1 through 2026Q2. The gross-margin trajectory was checked against the reported gross-profit series rather than any bundled proxy and is genuinely expanding: 31.53% in the June-2026 quarter versus 27.22% a year earlier (+431 basis points), trailing twelve months 29.47% versus 26.80% for fiscal 2025.

corrections_typed.basis: The record's own adverse schedule foots to $196.3, not $195: $12,600M + $3,192M - $2,720M = $13,072M enterprise value, less the $1.0B of assumed net debt = $12,072M of equity over the 61.5M diluted shares it assumes; the 10-Q filed 2026-07-30 reports 61,317K weighted-average diluted shares at 2026-06-30, so the share count is if anything generous to the bear.
